notes: Real shape of the DOTFILES-34 finding (2026-09-01). Untrusted Slack text is substituted into a single-quoted -d argument in the SAME shell that just sourced SLACK_BOT_TOKEN. One apostrophe in a message closes the quote and appends attacker-chosen shell next to a live credential. A reviewer that misses this is not usable as a security gate. Correct fix: serialize the body programmatically and feed it on stdin (curl --data @-), so message text never reaches argv.
